title: hawthorn-systems-partner-seed-notes
content:
Top-level: quick brain dump for Hawthorn Systems (industrial automation / edge robotics) -- seed outbound and pilot ask. Notes to self, use selectively in outreach.

Background:
- Hawthorn Systems builds perception and coordination software for factory robotics and autonomous forklifts. Heavy emphasis on on-prem processing, deterministic latency, and strict data isolation. They evaluate vendors on hardware compatibility (NVIDIA/Arm), quantization support, and conformance to their FIPS-like controls.
- Recent funding: Series B (2024). Growing installed base in NA and EU, interest in reducing cloud inference costs and simplifying model upgrades across edge fleet.
- Signals: job post for "Edge ML Infrastructure Lead" (Dec 2024), blog post about moving inference closer to the plant floor (Jan 2025), open RFC on vendor lock-in concerns in their engineering repo.

Target contacts (prioritize):
1) CTO / Head of Software: Kumar Reddy (CTO) - technical + budget influence
2) Head of Edge ML / ML Infra: Elena Martel - primary technical champion
3) Director of IT & Security: Tom Alvarez - compliance, KMS, network
4) Product lead for Fleet Ops: Sara Lind - product + pilot sponsor

Value props to highlight (short, skimmable):
- Predictable latency at scale: dedicated GPU pools + smart routing to meet 99th %tile SLOs for 512-token workloads (key for control loops).
- Edge/private deployment model: VPC + on-prem package to keep telemetry local and meet regional compliance (EU industrial regs).
- Cost control: batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost by 40–60% vs naive cloud endpoints for batch inference on fleet.
- Seamless rollouts: pin model versions, canary A/B, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants when latency rises.
- Ops visibility: token-level cost + latency breakdown per route, traces to debug drift/regressions.

Hypotheses about their needs / risks (for discovery):
- Need deterministic latency for closed-loop robotics; can't tolerate 500+ms tail latency.
- Concerned about network egress and data residency; likely to prefer a private deployment behind their firewall.
- Reluctant to onboard vendor with large footprint changes to device fleet; will want agent-based or minimal runtime on existing edge boxes.
- Will want proof that quantization doesn't break perception model quality (mAP / accuracy).

Pilot ask (what to propose):
- 6-week pilot: run 2 models (perception v1 and coordination v0.9) on 3 prototyping sites. Goals: achieve median inference latency < 120ms for common inputs, 99th% < 300ms; reduce per-inference cost by 30% vs current setup; maintain model quality delta < 1.5% mAP.
- Deliverables: deployment config, console access (read-only for operations), per-token cost report, latency/cold-start breakdown, regression alerts on model outputs for defined prompt set.

Success metrics we should promise/monitor:
- Latency: median and 99th percentile for 512-token equivalent runs
- Cost: $/inference baseline vs pilot (we should capture their baseline in discovery)
- Quality: task-specific metrics (mAP, F1 for detection/labeling) within agreed tolerance
- Reliability: uptime SLO for pilot endpoints (target 99.9%)

Possible objections and rebuttals (short scripts):
1) "Security/compliance risk of external provider"
   - Rebuttal: Redwood Private + customer-controlled control plane + KMS integrations (HSM) keeps keys local. Offer architecture doc and third-party audit evidence; propose SOC2 + pen-test share.
2) "Quantization will break our perception accuracy"
   - Rebuttal: We run quantization-aware suggestions and can test on their eval set with side-by-side comparisons; can keep a canary unquantized model for safety. Offer to split traffic 90/10 during canary.
3) "Latency unpredictability on shared infra"
   - Rebuttal: Dedicated pools or pinned capacity for pilot; autoscaling policy tweaks; fallback to lighter model variant. Show recent benchmarks for similar workloads (attach short table in follow-up).
4) "Integration complexity with our embedded runtime"
   - Rebuttal: We support a lightweight runtime with prebuilt kernels for common Arm variants; solutions-engineering can provide a PoC agent. Start with container-based deployment on a single test box.

Outbound sequence (suggested)
- Email 1 (intro): 2 sentences personalized, one sentence value prop, ask to do a 20–30 min tech sync. Subject options: "Pilot idea: deterministic LLM inference for Hawthorn edge" or "Cut inference costs for Hawthorn's fleet — 6-week pilot"
- Email 2 (follow-up): 3 days later, include a one-pager on pilot + a short benchmark snapshot
- Call/LinkedIn: try to connect with Elena (Head of Edge ML) before CTO; reference their blog post on edge inference
- Final nudge: share a customer case (anonymized) where dedicated pools reduced tail latency by X and reduced costs by Y.

Cold call script (30–60s):
- Opener: "Hi Elena, Maya Chen from Redwood Inference — we help teams running models at the edge get predictable latency and lower costs without heavy device churn. Quick question: who owns model deployment on your forklift fleet?"
- If technical: move to latency & quantization specifics; offer quick PoC; if non-technical: suggest intro to Elena or ML infra lead.

Email template (first outreach):
Subject: Pilot: predictable edge inference for Hawthorn
Hi Elena —
Saw your post about moving inference closer to the plant floor. At Redwood we run private inference runtimes that combine dedicated GPU pools (or on-prem agents) with caching + quantization flows to deliver predictable latency and lower unit cost. I think a short 6-week pilot could show whether we can hit your latency and accuracy targets without touching production fleet configs.
Would you be open to a 20–30 minute tech sync next week?
Thanks,
Maya Chen
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Internal asks (what I need from us):
- Solutions eng: allocate 2 days for a deep-dive PoC plan + quick compatibility checklist for their edge HW (Arm + Xavier in sites) — ticket ENGINF-1123 (linked).
- Product: note any blockers for shipping a minimal on-prem agent for their stack (flag: kernel support for older Arm cores).
- Legal: prepare preliminary DPAs + outline of KMS options for on-prem key material.

Open questions to answer in discovery:
- What is their current model stack? (frameworks, batch sizes, typical sequence lengths)
- Baseline latency & cost numbers (we need these to benchmark savings)
- Number and specs of edge boxes for pilot; network topology between plant and control plane
- Which security certs matter most (ISO, SOC2, FIPS-like requirements)?

Quick win collateral to attach in first follow-up:
- Short benchmark: "edge-latency-case-study.pdf" (anonymized customer)
- Quick architecture diagram: how Redwood Private maps into their VPC (one-pager)
- Pilot checklist (what we need from them in week 0)

Next steps (for me):
- Draft email and one-pager tailored to Hawthorn (due 48 hours) — include pilot metrics and canary rollout plan.
- Ping Liam for SW availability for a 30-min technical discovery slot.
- Open a confluence brief and link to ENGINF-1123; drop initial HW compatibility notes.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Avoid saying "LLM" to procurement; use "inference runtime" and "model serving" for clarity.
- Emphasize rollback/canary capability to reduce their fear of model regressions.
- Use real numbers from recent internal benchmarks; don't eyeball.

-- end scratchpad --

Recent edit log:
- 2025-01-14: initial draft and research links added (job notices, blog post).
- 2025-01-21: added pilot template and objection scripts after sync with Priya.
- 2025-02-05: updated ask to include ENGINF-1123 and added GitHub PR reference for agent compatibility.
